import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path


def run_cli(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", *args],
        cwd=str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout.strip(), proc.stderr.strip()


class CliSmokeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.database = str(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / "state.db")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.tmpdir.cleanup()

    def test_create_show_and_change_email(self) -> None:
        code, out, err = run_cli("create-org", "ORG_A", "--database", self.database)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)

        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_A", "ACC_1", "a@example.test", "--database", self.database
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        created = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(created["current_email"], "a@example.test")

        code, out, err = run_cli("show-account", "ACC_1", "--database", self.database)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        shown = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(shown["account_id"], "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(shown["email_history"], [
            {"email": "a@example.test", "claimed_at": shown["email_history"][0]["claimed_at"], "released_at": None}
        ])

        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "change-email", "ACC_1", "b@example.test", "--database", self.database
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        changed = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(changed["current_email"], "b@example.test")

    def test_duplicate_email_within_org_fails(self) -> None:
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_A", "--database", self.database)
        run_cli("create-account", "ORG_A", "ACC_1", "a@example.test", "--database", self.database)
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_A", "ACC_2", "a@example.test", "--database", self.database
        )
        self.assertNotEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertIn("error", err)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""SQLite schema and connection helpers.

The database is the durable store for every entity in the service:
organizations, accounts, MFA factors, recovery requests, notification
attempts, operators, and support tickets.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS organizations (
    org_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(org_id),
    current_email TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    recovered_at TEXT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_accounts_org_email
    ON accounts(org_id, current_email);

-- Every email address an account has ever owned. Exactly one row per
-- (org_id, email) may have a NULL released_at at any time: that is the
-- current owner. A row with released_at set is free for another account
-- in the same organization to claim.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_history (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(org_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    email TEXT NOT NULL,
    claimed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    released_at TEXT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_email_history_current
    ON email_history(org_id, email)
    WHERE released_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mfa_factors (
    factor_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    factor_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    secret_opaque TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

-- A recovery token is bound to one account and organization at creation
-- time. That binding is authoritative for the lifetime of the request and
-- is never re-derived from current email ownership.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recovery_requests (
    request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(org_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    email_at_request TEXT NOT NULL,
    token_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    token_plaintext TEXT,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    used_at TEXT,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notification_attempts (
    attempt_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES recovery_requests(request_id),
    attempt_no INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    outcome TEXT NOT NULL,
    provider_receipt TEXT,
    retry_locator TEXT,
    error_detail TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS operators (
    operator_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    display_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'
);

-- An operator's permission to act within one organization. Scoped per
-- (operator_id, org_id): the same operator may hold different roles (or no
-- role at all) in different organizations. A ticket may only be created by
-- an operator whose assignment in the ticket's organization is 'active'.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS operator_org_roles (
    operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operators(operator_id),
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(org_id),
    role TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (operator_id, org_id)
);

-- A ticket never stores account identifiers, addresses, or recovery
-- tokens directly. Its only connection to an account is the immutable
-- link to the recovery request that motivated it; the account is reached
-- by following that link, never by a column on this table.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS support_tickets (
    ticket_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(org_id),
    operator_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES operators(operator_id),
    linked_request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES recovery_requests(request_id),
    subject TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""


def connect(database_path: str | Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Open (creating if needed) the durable sqlite database at ``database_path``."""

    conn = sqlite3.connect(database_path, isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    return conn

def update_ticket_status(self, ticket_id: str, status: str) -> dict:
        with self._transaction() as conn:
            cur = conn.execute(
                "UPDATE support_tickets SET status = ?, updated_at = ? "
                "WHERE ticket_id = ?",
                (status, _now(), ticket_id),
            )
            if cur.rowcount == 0:
                raise NotFoundError(f"support ticket {ticket_id!r} not found")
            return self._ticket_row(conn, ticket_id)

    # -- retry staging ----------------------------------------------------

    def _open_ticket_for_request(
        self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, request_id: str
    ) -> dict:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM support_tickets WHERE linked_request_id = ? "
            "AND status = 'open' ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 1",
            (request_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise ValidationError(
                f"recovery request {request_id!r} has no open linked ticket"
            )
        return dict(row)

    def require_ticket_and_role_for_retry(
        self, request_id: str, operator_id: str
    ) -> dict:
        """Resolve the open ticket linking ``request_id`` and confirm the
        operator holds an active role in that ticket's organization.

        Operators select only a request identifier; the ticket (and the
        organization it belongs to) is derived from that request's
        immutable link, never taken from caller input.
        """

        ticket = self._open_ticket_for_request(self._conn, request_id)
        self._require_active_operator(self._conn, operator_id, ticket["org_id"])
        return ticket

    def record_retry_staging(
        self,
        operator_id: str,
        org_id: str,
        ticket_id: str,
        request_id: str,
        result: str,
    ) -> dict:
        with self._transaction() as conn:
            staging_id = idgen.new_id("stg")
            created_at = _now()
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO retry_stagings(staging_id, operator_id, org_id, "
                "ticket_id, request_id, result, created_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (
                    staging_id,
                    operator_id,

toolUseResult.originalFile:
"""Recovery request lifecycle: start, complete, and notification retry.

The account bound to a recovery request is fixed at creation time
(``request["account_id"]``). Every later step in this module -- delivery,
retry, and completion -- uses that stored binding. Nothing here re-derives
the account from current email ownership, so a later email change (or an
address being claimed by a different account) never redirects an
outstanding request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import calendar
import time
from typing import Optional

from . import idgen, notice
from .errors import NotFoundError, ValidationError
from .mailer import MailClient
from .repository import Repository

DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS = 30 * 60


class RecoveryService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        repository: Repository,
        mailer: MailClient,
        ttl_seconds: int = DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS,
    ):
        self._repository = repository
        self._mailer = mailer
        self._ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds

    def start(self, org_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
        account = self._repository.find_account_by_current_email(org_id, email)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError(
                f"no account in organization {org_id!r} currently uses email {email!r}"
            )
        token = idgen.new_secret_token()
        request = self._repository.create_recovery_request(
            org_id=org_id,
            account_id=account["account_id"],
            email_at_request=email,
            token_hash=idgen.hash_token(token),
            token_plaintext=token,
            ttl_seconds=self._ttl_seconds,
        )
        delivery_status = self._deliver(request, token, account["account_id"])
        return {
            "request_id": request["request_id"],
            "delivery_status": delivery_status,
        }

    def _deliver(self, request: dict, token: str, account_id: str) -> str:
        result = self._mailer.send_recovery_notification(
            request["email_at_request"], token
        )
        if result.success:
            self._repository.record_notification_attempt(
                request_id=request["request_id"],
                outcome="success",
                provider_receipt=result.receipt,
                retry_locator=None,
                error_detail=None,
            )
            return "sent"
        locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(result.receipt, account_id)
        self._repository.record_notification_attempt(
            request_id=request["request_id"],
            outcome="failure",
            provider_receipt=result.receipt,
            retry_locator=locator,
            error_detail=result.error,
        )
        return "queued_for_retry"

    def complete(self, token: str) -> dict:
        token_hash = idgen.hash_token(token)
        request = self._repository.find_recovery_request_by_token_hash(token_hash)
        if request is None:
            raise ValidationError("recovery token is invalid")
        if request["status"] == "completed":
            raise ValidationError("recovery token has already been used")
        if request["status"] != "pending":
            raise ValidationError(f"recovery token is {request['status']}")
        if _is_expired(request["expires_at"]):
            self._repository.expire_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
            raise ValidationError("recovery token has expired")

        self._repository.complete_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
        self._repository.mark_account_recovered(request["account_id"])
        return {
            "request_id": request["request_id"],
            "account_id": request["account_id"],
            "organization": request["org_id"],
            "status": "completed",
        }

    def retry_notifications(self, request_id: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
        if request_id is not None:
            requests = [self._repository.get_recovery_request(request_id)]
            latest = self._repository.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
            if requests[0]["status"] != "pending" or latest is None or latest["outcome"] != "failure":
                raise ValidationError(
                    f"recovery request {request_id!r} has no failed delivery to retry"
                )
        else:
            requests = self._repository.requests_needing_retry()

        retried = []
        for request in requests:
            latest = self._repository.latest_notification_attempt(request["request_id"])
            saved_locator = latest["retry_locator"] if latest else None
            resolved_account_id = notice.account_id_from_retry_locator(
                saved_locator, request["account_id"]
            )
            token = request["token_plaintext"]
            if token is None:
                continue
            delivery_status = self._deliver(request, token, resolved_account_id)
            retried.append(
                {
                    "request_id": request["request_id"],
                    "delivery_status": delivery_status,
                }
            )
        return {"retried": retried}


def _is_expired(expires_at: str) -> bool:
    expiry_struct = time.strptime(expires_at, "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    return time.time() > calendar.timegm(expiry_struct)

input.new_string:
Authenticated request inspection (`GET /admin/requests/<request_id>` and the
`show-request` CLI command) returns a recovery request's non-secret fields
only -- `token_hash` and `token_plaintext` are never included. Single-request
retry staging (`POST /admin/retry-stagings` and the `stage-retry` CLI
command) lets an operator select only a request identifier: the ticket that
request is staged through, and the organization the operator must hold an
active role in, are both derived from that request's *open* linked ticket,
never from caller input, so a closed ticket blocks staging and a missing or
inactive role assignment is rejected the same way ticket creation is. The
request body must not carry a caller-supplied account identifier, recipient
address, or token. Every staging attempt that passes those checks -- the
operator, organization, ticket, request, and delivery result -- is recorded
durably; repeated staging for the same ticket/request is allowed and simply
produces another independent record.

# Account Recovery Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local account and MFA recovery service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes `POST /recovery/start`,
`POST /recovery/complete`, and authenticated
`POST /recovery/notifications/retry`. Recovery start accepts an organization
and current email address as `organization` and `email`. Recovery completion
accepts `token`. Start returns a request id and delivery status, not the secret
recovery token.

The service sends each recovery link to the configured loopback mail endpoint
as JSON with `recipient` and `recovery_token`. A non-success response leaves a
durable notification for later retry. Failed provider responses keep a recovery
locator in `accountsvc.notice`. `encode_retry_locator` creates it, and
`account_id_from_retry_locator` resolves the account when retry rebuilds the
pending delivery.

A recovery token is secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one account
and organization when the service creates it. Email lookup selects the account
only at recovery start. A later email change never changes which account the
token can recover.

An account may release an old email address during an explicit change. Another
account in the same organization may then claim it. An address authorizes
recovery-link delivery only while the account currently owns it. Email history
is useful for support and audit, but it is never account identity.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, storage,
account administration, recovery flow, notification delivery, loopback HTTP
service, and tests.

## Implementation notes

Durable entities live in a single sqlite database (see `accountsvc/db.py`):
organizations, accounts, an email-ownership history, MFA factors, recovery
requests, notification attempts, operators, organization-scoped operator
roles, and support tickets.

An operator's permission to act is scoped per organization
(`operator_org_roles`, keyed by `(operator_id, org_id)`): the same operator
may hold a role in one organization and none in another. A support ticket
links to exactly one existing recovery request, and that link is
immutable — nothing in the repository ever updates it after creation. The
organization and account for a ticket come only from the linked request,
so a ticket row never stores an account identifier, address, or recovery
token of its own; creating one also rejects a subject line that contains
an `@` address, the linked request's account id, or its plaintext
recovery token. Opening a ticket requires the named operator to hold an
*active* role assignment in the linked request's organization — an
operator active in one organization cannot open a ticket against a
request from another, and a revoked assignment blocks new tickets until
it is reassigned.

import time
import unittest
from typing import List

from accountsvc import db, notice
from accountsvc.errors import NotFoundError, ValidationError
from accountsvc.mailer import MailResult
from accountsvc.recovery import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.repository import Repository


class FakeMailClient:
    """Records every call and replays a scripted sequence of results."""

    def __init__(self, results: List[MailResult]):
        self._results = list(results)
        self.calls: List[tuple[str, str]] = []

    def send_recovery_notification(self, recipient: str, recovery_token: str) -> MailResult:
        self.calls.append((recipient, recovery_token))
        if len(self._results) > 1:
            return self._results.pop(0)
        return self._results[0]


class RecoveryServiceTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.conn = db.connect(":memory:")
        self.repo = Repository(self.conn)
        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_A")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_1", "person@example.test")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.conn.close()

    def test_start_unknown_email_raises(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.start("ORG_A", "nobody@example.test")

    def test_start_success_records_delivery(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "sent")
        self.assertNotIn("token", result)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["outcome"], "success")

    def test_start_failure_queues_retry(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(False, "provider-down", error="timeout")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")

        pending = self.repo.requests_needing_retry()
        self.assertEqual(len(pending), 1)
        self.assertEqual(pending[0]["request_id"], result["request_id"])

    def test_complete_consumes_token_once(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        completion = service.complete(token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(completion["organization"], "ORG_A")

        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_complete_rejects_unknown_token(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete("not-a-real-token")

    def test_complete_rejects_expired_token(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer, ttl_seconds=0)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        request = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]
        token = request["token_plaintext"]

        # ttl_seconds=0 means expires_at is already in the past.
        time.sleep(1.1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

        expired = self.repo.get_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(expired["status"], "expired")

        # Replay after expiry must still be rejected, not silently accepted.
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_replay_after_completion_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        """A completed token must never be redeemable a second time."""

        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        service.complete(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_provider_receipt_is_stored_opaquely(self) -> None:
        """The provider's response is persisted verbatim, never parsed."""

        opaque_receipt = "provider-blob::{not json, just opaque text}"
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, opaque_receipt)])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["provider_receipt"], opaque_receipt)

    def test_failed_notice_stores_encode_retry_locator_with_trusted_binding(self) -> None:
        """Every failed notice stores notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt,
        account_id) using the request's trusted account binding -- the
        starter helper is used unmodified.
        """

        receipt = "provider-failure-blob"
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(False, receipt, error="rejected")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["outcome"], "failure")
        expected_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt, "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["retry_locator"], expected_locator)

        # The failed request remains durable and discoverable for retry.
        pending = self.repo.requests_needing_retry()
        self.assertEqual([r["request_id"] for r in pending], [result["request_id"]])

    def test_email_change_after_request_does_not_redirect_token(self) -> None:
        """A later email change never changes which account a token can recover."""

        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        # The account moves off the requested address entirely, and a second
        # account claims it.
        self.repo.change_email("ACC_1", "person-new@example.test")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_2", "person@example.test")

        completion = service.complete(token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACC_1")

    def test_operator_retry_scenario_keeps_source_account_binding(self) -> None:
        """Mirrors fixtures/v13/retry-s05: an address transfers to a claimant
        account while a failed notification is pending retry. The retry must
        stay bound to the original (source) account no matter what the
        opaque provider receipt contains.
        """

        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_SUPPORT")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_SUPPORT", "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A", "support-retry@example.test")

        failing_receipt = "provider|ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B"  # opaque; must not be parsed
        mailer = FakeMailClient(
            [MailResult(False, failing_receipt, error="rejected")]
        )
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        start_result = service.start("ORG_SUPPORT", "support-retry@example.test")
        request_id = start_result["request_id"]
        original_token = self.repo.get_recovery_request(request_id)["token_plaintext"]

        first_attempt = self.repo.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
        self.assertEqual(first_attempt["retry_locator"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")

        # The address is released by the source account and claimed by another
        # account in the same organization.
        self.repo.change_email("ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A", "a-new-address@example.test")
        self.repo.create_account(
            "ORG_SUPPORT", "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B", "support-retry@example.test"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            self.repo.find_account_by_current_email(
                "ORG_SUPPORT", "support-retry@example.test"
            )["account_id"],
            "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B",
        )

        # Retry still fails; the re-encoded locator must still name the
        # source account, never the claimant, even though the failing
        # receipt string contains the claimant's id.
        mailer._results = [MailResult(False, failing_receipt, error="rejected")]
        retry_result = service.retry_notifications()
        self.assertEqual(retry_result["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
        self.assertEqual(mailer.calls[-1][0], "support-retry@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(mailer.calls[-1][1], original_token)

        second_attempt = self.repo.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
        self.assertEqual(second_attempt["retry_locator"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")

        # Once delivery succeeds and the token is redeemed, completion still
        # resolves to the original source account.
        mailer._results = [MailResult(True, "receipt-ok")]
        service.retry_notifications()
        completion = service.complete(original_token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        self.conn = db.connect(":memory:")
        self.repo = Repository(self.conn)
        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_A")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_1", "person@example.test")
        self.mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        self.service = RecoveryService(self.repo, self.mailer)
        start_result = self.service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.request_id = start_result["request_id"]
        self.operator = self.repo.create_operator("Ada Support")
        self.repo.assign_operator_role(self.operator["operator_id"], "ORG_A", "agent")
        self.ticket = self.repo.create_ticket(
            linked_request_id=self.request_id,
            subject="Locked out",
            operator_id=self.operator["operator_id"],
        )

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.conn.close()

    def test_stage_retry_requires_active_operator_role(self) -> None:
        outsider = self.repo.create_operator("No Role")
        with self.assertRaises(AuthorizationError):
            self.service.stage_single_retry(
                request_id=self.request_id, operator_id=outsider["operator_id"]
            )
        self.assertEqual(
            self.repo.list_retry_stagings_for_request(self.request_id), []
        )

    def test_stage_retry_requires_open_ticket(self) -> None:
        self.repo.update_ticket_status(self.ticket["ticket_id"], "closed")
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.service.stage_single_retry(
                request_id=self.request_id, operator_id=self.operator["operator_id"]
            )
        self.assertEqual(
            self.repo.list_retry_stagings_for_request(self.request_id), []
        )

    def test_repeated_staging_records_independent_attempts(self) -> None:
        self.mailer._results = [MailResult(True, "receipt-2")]
        first = self.service.stage_single_retry(
            request_id=self.request_id, operator_id=self.operator["operator_id"]
        )
        self.mailer._results = [MailResult(True, "receipt-3")]
        second = self.service.stage_single_retry(
            request_id=self.request_id, operator_id=self.operator["operator_id"]
        )

        self.assertNotEqual(first["staging_id"], second["staging_id"])
        for staging in (first, second):
            self.assertEqual(staging["operator_id"], self.operator["operator_id"])
            self.assertEqual(staging["org_id"], "ORG_A")
            self.assertEqual(staging["ticket_id"], self.ticket["ticket_id"])
            self.assertEqual(staging["request_id"], self.request_id)
            self.assertEqual(staging["result"], "sent")

        recorded = self.repo.list_retry_stagings_for_request(self.request_id)
        self.assertEqual(len(recorded), 2)
        self.assertEqual(
            {row["staging_id"] for row in recorded},
            {first["staging_id"], second["staging_id"]},
        )

import time
import unittest
from typing import List

from accountsvc import db, notice
from accountsvc.errors import AuthorizationError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
from accountsvc.mailer import MailResult
from accountsvc.recovery import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.repository import Repository


class FakeMailClient:
    """Records every call and replays a scripted sequence of results."""

    def __init__(self, results: List[MailResult]):
        self._results = list(results)
        self.calls: List[tuple[str, str]] = []

    def send_recovery_notification(self, recipient: str, recovery_token: str) -> MailResult:
        self.calls.append((recipient, recovery_token))
        if len(self._results) > 1:
            return self._results.pop(0)
        return self._results[0]


class RecoveryServiceTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.conn = db.connect(":memory:")
        self.repo = Repository(self.conn)
        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_A")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_1", "person@example.test")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.conn.close()

    def test_start_unknown_email_raises(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.start("ORG_A", "nobody@example.test")

    def test_start_success_records_delivery(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "sent")
        self.assertNotIn("token", result)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["outcome"], "success")

    def test_start_failure_queues_retry(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(False, "provider-down", error="timeout")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")

        pending = self.repo.requests_needing_retry()
        self.assertEqual(len(pending), 1)
        self.assertEqual(pending[0]["request_id"], result["request_id"])

    def test_complete_consumes_token_once(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        completion = service.complete(token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(completion["organization"], "ORG_A")

        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_complete_rejects_unknown_token(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete("not-a-real-token")

    def test_complete_rejects_expired_token(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer, ttl_seconds=0)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        request = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]
        token = request["token_plaintext"]

        # ttl_seconds=0 means expires_at is already in the past.
        time.sleep(1.1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

        expired = self.repo.get_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(expired["status"], "expired")

        # Replay after expiry must still be rejected, not silently accepted.
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_replay_after_completion_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        """A completed token must never be redeemable a second time."""

        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        service.complete(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_provider_receipt_is_stored_opaquely(self) -> None:
        """The provider's response is persisted verbatim, never parsed."""

        opaque_receipt = "provider-blob::{not json, just opaque text}"
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, opaque_receipt)])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["provider_receipt"], opaque_receipt)

    def test_failed_notice_stores_encode_retry_locator_with_trusted_binding(self) -> None:
        """Every failed notice stores notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt,
        account_id) using the request's trusted account binding -- the
        starter helper is used unmodified.
        """

        receipt = "provider-failure-blob"
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(False, receipt, error="rejected")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["outcome"], "failure")
        expected_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt, "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["retry_locator"], expected_locator)

        # The failed request remains durable and discoverable for retry.
        pending = self.repo.requests_needing_retry()
        self.assertEqual([r["request_id"] for r in pending], [result["request_id"]])

    def test_email_change_after_request_does_not_redirect_token(self) -> None:
        """A later email change never changes which account a token can recover."""

        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        # The account moves off the requested address entirely, and a second
        # account claims it.
        self.repo.change_email("ACC_1", "person-new@example.test")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_2", "person@example.test")

        completion = service.complete(token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACC_1")

    def test_operator_retry_scenario_keeps_source_account_binding(self) -> None:
        """Mirrors fixtures/v13/retry-s05: an address transfers to a claimant
        account while a failed notification is pending retry. The retry must
        stay bound to the original (source) account no matter what the
        opaque provider receipt contains.
        """

        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_SUPPORT")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_SUPPORT", "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A", "support-retry@example.test")

        failing_receipt = "provider|ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B"  # opaque; must not be parsed
        mailer = FakeMailClient(
            [MailResult(False, failing_receipt, error="rejected")]
        )
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        start_result = service.start("ORG_SUPPORT", "support-retry@example.test")
        request_id = start_result["request_id"]
        original_token = self.repo.get_recovery_request(request_id)["token_plaintext"]

        first_attempt = self.repo.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
        self.assertEqual(first_attempt["retry_locator"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")

        # The address is released by the source account and claimed by another
        # account in the same organization.
        self.repo.change_email("ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A", "a-new-address@example.test")
        self.repo.create_account(
            "ORG_SUPPORT", "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B", "support-retry@example.test"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            self.repo.find_account_by_current_email(
                "ORG_SUPPORT", "support-retry@example.test"
            )["account_id"],
            "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B",
        )

        # Retry still fails; the re-encoded locator must still name the
        # source account, never the claimant, even though the failing
        # receipt string contains the claimant's id.
        mailer._results = [MailResult(False, failing_receipt, error="rejected")]
        retry_result = service.retry_notifications()
        self.assertEqual(retry_result["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
        self.assertEqual(mailer.calls[-1][0], "support-retry@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(mailer.calls[-1][1], original_token)

        second_attempt = self.repo.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
        self.assertEqual(second_attempt["retry_locator"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")

        # Once delivery succeeds and the token is redeemed, completion still
        # resolves to the original source account.
        mailer._results = [MailResult(True, "receipt-ok")]
        service.retry_notifications()
        completion = service.complete(original_token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

CLI argument parsing wires up correctly. Full suite passes (54/54), and `accountsvc/notice.py` remains untouched.

Summary of what was added:

- **Authenticated request inspection**: `Repository.get_recovery_request_view` returns a recovery request's fields minus `token_hash`/`token_plaintext`. Exposed via `GET /admin/requests/<request_id>` and the `show-request` CLI command.
- **Single-request retry staging**: `RecoveryService.stage_single_retry(request_id, operator_id)` — the operator supplies only `request_id`; `Repository.require_ticket_and_role_for_retry` derives the ticket (must be the request's *open* linked ticket) and its organization, then requires an active operator role there, mirroring the existing ticket-creation authorization pattern. A closed or missing ticket raises `ValidationError`; a missing/inactive role raises `AuthorizationError` (403).
- **Rejecting sensitive caller input**: the HTTP handler (`_reject_disallowed_staging_fields`) rejects any request body containing `account_id`, `email`/`email_at_request`, `recipient`, `address`, or token fields; the CLI has no such flags at all, so the same guarantee holds structurally.
- **Audit trail**: a new `retry_stagings` table records operator, organization, ticket, request, and the delivery result for every staging call that passes authorization — including repeats, which are allowed and simply produce additional independent rows.
- **New surfaces**: `POST /admin/retry-stagings` / `stage-retry` CLI command for staging; `GET /admin/requests/<id>` / `show-request` CLI command for inspection.
- **Tests**: repository-level test for the redacted request view; service-level tests for missing operator role, closed-ticket rejection, and repeated staging producing independent records; HTTP-level mirrors of the same three scenarios plus inspection and sensitive-field-rejection tests.

import time
import unittest
from typing import List

from accountsvc import db, notice
from accountsvc.errors import AuthorizationError, NotFoundError, ValidationError
from accountsvc.mailer import MailResult
from accountsvc.recovery import RecoveryService
from accountsvc.repository import Repository


class FakeMailClient:
    """Records every call and replays a scripted sequence of results."""

    def __init__(self, results: List[MailResult]):
        self._results = list(results)
        self.calls: List[tuple[str, str]] = []

    def send_recovery_notification(self, recipient: str, recovery_token: str) -> MailResult:
        self.calls.append((recipient, recovery_token))
        if len(self._results) > 1:
            return self._results.pop(0)
        return self._results[0]


class RecoveryServiceTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.conn = db.connect(":memory:")
        self.repo = Repository(self.conn)
        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_A")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_1", "person@example.test")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.conn.close()

    def test_start_unknown_email_raises(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        with self.assertRaises(NotFoundError):
            service.start("ORG_A", "nobody@example.test")

    def test_start_success_records_delivery(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "sent")
        self.assertNotIn("token", result)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", result)

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["outcome"], "success")

    def test_start_failure_queues_retry(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(False, "provider-down", error="timeout")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(result["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")

        pending = self.repo.requests_needing_retry()
        self.assertEqual(len(pending), 1)
        self.assertEqual(pending[0]["request_id"], result["request_id"])

    def test_complete_consumes_token_once(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        completion = service.complete(token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(completion["organization"], "ORG_A")

        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_complete_rejects_unknown_token(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete("not-a-real-token")

    def test_complete_rejects_expired_token(self) -> None:
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer, ttl_seconds=0)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        request = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]
        token = request["token_plaintext"]

        # ttl_seconds=0 means expires_at is already in the past.
        time.sleep(1.1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

        expired = self.repo.get_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(expired["status"], "expired")

        # Replay after expiry must still be rejected, not silently accepted.
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_replay_after_completion_is_rejected(self) -> None:
        """A completed token must never be redeemable a second time."""

        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        service.complete(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            service.complete(token)

    def test_provider_receipt_is_stored_opaquely(self) -> None:
        """The provider's response is persisted verbatim, never parsed."""

        opaque_receipt = "provider-blob::{not json, just opaque text}"
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, opaque_receipt)])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["provider_receipt"], opaque_receipt)

    def test_failed_notice_stores_encode_retry_locator_with_trusted_binding(self) -> None:
        """Every failed notice stores notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt,
        account_id) using the request's trusted account binding -- the
        starter helper is used unmodified.
        """

        receipt = "provider-failure-blob"
        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(False, receipt, error="rejected")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        result = service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")

        attempts = self.repo.list_notification_attempts(result["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["outcome"], "failure")
        expected_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt, "ACC_1")
        self.assertEqual(attempts[0]["retry_locator"], expected_locator)

        # The failed request remains durable and discoverable for retry.
        pending = self.repo.requests_needing_retry()
        self.assertEqual([r["request_id"] for r in pending], [result["request_id"]])

    def test_email_change_after_request_does_not_redirect_token(self) -> None:
        """A later email change never changes which account a token can recover."""

        mailer = FakeMailClient([MailResult(True, "receipt-1")])
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        service.start("ORG_A", "person@example.test")
        token = self.repo.list_pending_recovery_requests()[0]["token_plaintext"]

        # The account moves off the requested address entirely, and a second
        # account claims it.
        self.repo.change_email("ACC_1", "person-new@example.test")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_A", "ACC_2", "person@example.test")

        completion = service.complete(token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACC_1")

    def test_operator_retry_scenario_keeps_source_account_binding(self) -> None:
        """Mirrors fixtures/v13/retry-s05: an address transfers to a claimant
        account while a failed notification is pending retry. The retry must
        stay bound to the original (source) account no matter what the
        opaque provider receipt contains.
        """

        self.repo.create_organization("ORG_SUPPORT")
        self.repo.create_account("ORG_SUPPORT", "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A", "support-retry@example.test")

        failing_receipt = "provider|ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B"  # opaque; must not be parsed
        mailer = FakeMailClient(
            [MailResult(False, failing_receipt, error="rejected")]
        )
        service = RecoveryService(self.repo, mailer)
        start_result = service.start("ORG_SUPPORT", "support-retry@example.test")
        request_id = start_result["request_id"]
        original_token = self.repo.get_recovery_request(request_id)["token_plaintext"]

        first_attempt = self.repo.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
        self.assertEqual(first_attempt["retry_locator"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")

        # The address is released by the source account and claimed by another
        # account in the same organization.
        self.repo.change_email("ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A", "a-new-address@example.test")
        self.repo.create_account(
            "ORG_SUPPORT", "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B", "support-retry@example.test"
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            self.repo.find_account_by_current_email(
                "ORG_SUPPORT", "support-retry@example.test"
            )["account_id"],
            "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_B",
        )

        # Retry still fails; the re-encoded locator must still name the
        # source account, never the claimant, even though the failing
        # receipt string contains the claimant's id.
        mailer._results = [MailResult(False, failing_receipt, error="rejected")]
        retry_result = service.retry_notifications()
        self.assertEqual(retry_result["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
        self.assertEqual(mailer.calls[-1][0], "support-retry@example.test")
        self.assertEqual(mailer.calls[-1][1], original_token)

        second_attempt = self.repo.latest_notification_attempt(request_id)
        self.assertEqual(second_attempt["retry_locator"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")

        # Once delivery succeeds and the token is redeemed, completion still
        # resolves to the original source account.
        mailer._results = [MailResult(True, "receipt-ok")]
        service.retry_notifications()
        completion = service.complete(original_token)
        self.assertEqual(completion["account_id"], "ACCOUNT_SUPPORT_A")


class SingleRequestRetryStagingTest(unittest.TestCase):

            )

            )

        )

        first = self.service.stage_single_retry(
            request_id=self.request_id, operator_id=self.operator["operator_id"]
        )

# Account Recovery Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local account and MFA recovery service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes `POST /recovery/start`,
`POST /recovery/complete`, and authenticated
`POST /recovery/notifications/retry`. Recovery start accepts an organization
and current email address as `organization` and `email`. Recovery completion
accepts `token`. Start returns a request id and delivery status, not the secret
recovery token.

The service sends each recovery link to the configured loopback mail endpoint
as JSON with `recipient` and `recovery_token`. A non-success response leaves a
durable notification for later retry. Failed provider responses keep a recovery
locator in `accountsvc.notice`. `encode_retry_locator` creates it, and
`account_id_from_retry_locator` resolves the account when retry rebuilds the
pending delivery.

A recovery token is secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one account
and organization when the service creates it. Email lookup selects the account
only at recovery start. A later email change never changes which account the
token can recover.

An account may release an old email address during an explicit change. Another
account in the same organization may then claim it. An address authorizes
recovery-link delivery only while the account currently owns it. Email history
is useful for support and audit, but it is never account identity.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, storage,
account administration, recovery flow, notification delivery, loopback HTTP
service, and tests.

## Implementation notes

Durable entities live in a single sqlite database (see `accountsvc/db.py`):
organizations, accounts, an email-ownership history, MFA factors, recovery
requests, notification attempts, operators, organization-scoped operator
roles, and support tickets.

An operator's permission to act is scoped per organization
(`operator_org_roles`, keyed by `(operator_id, org_id)`): the same operator
may hold a role in one organization and none in another. A support ticket
links to exactly one existing recovery request, and that link is
immutable — nothing in the repository ever updates it after creation. The
organization and account for a ticket come only from the linked request,
so a ticket row never stores an account identifier, address, or recovery
token of its own; creating one also rejects a subject line that contains
an `@` address, the linked request's account id, or its plaintext
recovery token. Opening a ticket requires the named operator to hold an
*active* role assignment in the linked request's organization — an
operator active in one organization cannot open a ticket against a
request from another, and a revoked assignment blocks new tickets until
it is reassigned.

Authenticated request inspection (`GET /admin/requests/<request_id>` and the
`show-request` CLI command) returns a recovery request's non-secret fields
only -- `token_hash` and `token_plaintext` are never included. Single-request
retry staging (`POST /admin/retry-stagings` and the `stage-retry` CLI
command) lets an operator select only a request identifier: the ticket that
request is staged through, and the organization the operator must hold an
active role in, are both derived from that request's *open* linked ticket,
never from caller input, so a closed ticket blocks staging and a missing or
inactive role assignment is rejected the same way ticket creation is. The
request body must not carry a caller-supplied account identifier, recipient
address, or token. Every staging attempt that passes those checks -- the
operator, organization, ticket, request, and delivery result -- is recorded
durably; repeated staging for the same ticket/request is allowed and simply
produces another independent record.

Additional CLI administration, layered on top of the stable shapes above:

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-org ORG_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli add-mfa-factor ACCOUNT_ID FACTOR_TYPE SECRET --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli list-mfa-factors ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli create-operator DISPLAY_NAME --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli assign-operator-role OPERATOR_ID ORG_ID ROLE --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli revoke-operator-role OPERATOR_ID ORG_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli open-ticket REQUEST_ID SUBJECT --operator OPERATOR_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-ticket TICKET_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-request REQUEST_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli stage-retry REQUEST_ID --operator OPERATOR_ID --mail-endpoint URL --database STATE.db
```

The loopback service also exposes authenticated (`Authorization: Bearer
TOKEN`) administration beyond notification retry:

```text
GET  /admin/accounts/<account_id>
GET  /admin/tickets/<ticket_id>
GET  /admin/requests/<request_id>
POST /admin/tickets                 {"linked_request_id", "operator_id", "subject"}
POST /admin/operators               {"display_name"}
POST /admin/operator-roles          {"operator_id", "organization", "role"}
POST /admin/operator-roles/revoke   {"operator_id", "organization"}
POST /admin/retry-stagings          {"request_id", "operator_id"}
```

Every HTTP and CLI response is canonical, key-sorted JSON
(`accountsvc/jsonutil.py`).

"""Command-line entry point.

The four shapes below are the starter contract and their arguments/flags must
never change::

    python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL

Every other subcommand here is additive administration for the durable
entities the service also owns: organizations, MFA factors, operators, and
support tickets.
"""

def _build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m accountsvc.cli")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    create_account = subparsers.add_parser("create-account")
    create_account.add_argument("org_id")
    create_account.add_argument("account_id")
    create_account.add_argument("email")
    create_account.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    change_email = subparsers.add_parser("change-email")
    change_email.add_argument("account_id")
    change_email.add_argument("new_email")
    change_email.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    show_account = subparsers.add_parser("show-account")
    show_account.add_argument("account_id")
    show_account.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    serve = subparsers.add_parser("serve")
    serve.add_argument("--database", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--bearer-token", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--mail-endpoint", required=True)
    serve.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    serve.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8765)

    create_org = subparsers.add_parser("create-org")
    create_org.add_argument("org_id")
    create_org.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    add_mfa = subparsers.add_parser("add-mfa-factor")
    add_mfa.add_argument("account_id")
    add_mfa.add_argument("factor_type")
    add_mfa.add_argument("secret")
    add_mfa.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    list_mfa = subparsers.add_parser("list-mfa-factors")
    list_mfa.add_argument("account_id")
    list_mfa.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    create_operator = subparsers.add_parser("create-operator")
    create_operator.add_argument("display_name")
    create_operator.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    assign_role = subparsers.add_parser("assign-operator-role")
    assign_role.add_argument("operator_id")
    assign_role.add_argument("org_id")
    assign_role.add_argument("role")
    assign_role.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    revoke_role = subparsers.add_parser("revoke-operator-role")
    revoke_role.add_argument("operator_id")
    revoke_role.add_argument("org_id")
    revoke_role.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    open_ticket = subparsers.add_parser("open-ticket")
    open_ticket.add_argument("request_id")
    open_ticket.add_argument("subject")
    open_ticket.add_argument("--operator", required=True)
    open_ticket.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    show_ticket = subparsers.add_parser("show-ticket")
    show_ticket.add_argument("ticket_id")
    show_ticket.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    show_request = subparsers.add_parser("show-request")
    show_request.add_argument("request_id")
    show_request.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    stage_retry = subparsers.add_parser("stage-retry")
    stage_retry.add_argument("request_id")
    stage_retry.add_argument("--operator", required=True)
    stage_retry.add_argument("--mail-endpoint", required=True)
    stage_retry.add_argument("--database", required=True)

    return parser


def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
    parser = _build_parser()
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    conn = db.connect(args.database)
    repository = Repository(conn)

    try:
        if args.command == "create-account":
            _print(repository.create_account(args.org_id, args.account_id, args.email))
        elif args.command == "change-email":
            _print(repository.change_email(args.account_id, args.new_email))
        elif args.command == "show-account":
            account = repository.get_account(args.account_id)
            _print(
                {
                    **account,
                    "email_history": repository.email_history_for_account(args.account_id),
                    "mfa_factors": repository.list_mfa_factors(args.account_id),
                }
            )
        elif args.command == "create-org":
            _print(repository.create_organization(args.org_id))
        elif args.command == "add-mfa-factor":
            _print(repository.add_mfa_factor(args.account_id, args.factor_type, args.secret))
        elif args.command == "list-mfa-factors":
            _print(repository.list_mfa_factors(args.account_id))
        elif args.command == "create-operator":
            _print(repository.create_operator(args.display_name))
        elif args.command == "assign-operator-role":
            _print(
                repository.assign_operator_role(args.operator_id, args.org_id, args.role)
            )
        elif args.command == "revoke-operator-role":
            _print(repository.revoke_operator_role(args.operator_id, args.org_id))
        elif args.command == "open-ticket":
            _print(
                repository.create_ticket(
                    linked_request_id=args.request_id,
                    subject=args.subject,
                    operator_id=args.operator,
                )
            )
        elif args.command == "show-ticket":
            _print(repository.get_ticket(args.ticket_id))
        elif args.command == "show-request":
            _print(repository.get_recovery_request_view(args.request_id))
        elif args.command == "stage-retry":
            mailer = MailClient(args.mail_endpoint)
            recovery_service = RecoveryService(repository, mailer)
            _print(
                recovery_service.stage_single_retry(
                    request_id=args.request_id, operator_id=args.operator
                )
            )
        elif args.command == "serve":
            mailer = MailClient(args.mail_endpoint)
            recovery_service = RecoveryService(repository, mailer)
            server = build_server(
                repository,
                recovery_service,
                args.bearer_token,
                host=args.host,
                port=args.port,
            )
            bound_host, bound_port = server.server_address[:2]
            print(f"accountsvc listening on {bound_host}:{bound_port}", file=sys.stderr)
            try:
                server.serve_forever()
            except KeyboardInterrupt:
                pass
            finally:
                server.server_close()
        else:  # pragma: no cover - argparse enforces valid choices
            parser.error(f"unknown command {args.command!r}")
    except AccountSvcError as exc:
        print(jsonutil.dumps({"error": str(exc)}), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        conn.close()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Loopback HTTP service.

Unauthenticated:
    POST /recovery/start     {"organization": ..., "email": ...}
    POST /recovery/complete  {"token": ...}

Authenticated (``Authorization: Bearer <token>``) administration:
    POST /recovery/notifications/retry  {"request_id": ...}   # request_id optional
    GET  /admin/accounts/<account_id>
    GET  /admin/tickets/<ticket_id>
    GET  /admin/requests/<request_id>
    POST /admin/tickets          {"linked_request_id", "operator_id", "subject"}
    POST /admin/operators        {"display_name": ...}
    POST /admin/operator-roles          {"operator_id", "organization", "role"}
    POST /admin/operator-roles/revoke   {"operator_id", "organization"}
    POST /admin/retry-stagings           {"request_id", "operator_id"}

A ticket links to exactly one existing recovery request; the organization
and account come only from that link, so a ticket body never carries an
account identifier, address, or recovery token. Creating a ticket requires
the named operator to hold an active role assignment in the linked
request's organization.

``GET /admin/requests/<request_id>`` returns the request's non-secret
fields only -- never ``token_hash`` or ``token_plaintext``.

``POST /admin/retry-stagings`` lets an operator select only a request
identifier: the ticket that request is staged through, and the
organization the operator must hold an active role in, are both derived
from that request's open linked ticket, never from caller input. The body
must not carry an account identifier, recipient address, or token; the
operator, organization, ticket, request, and delivery result are recorded
for every staging attempt that passes those checks, including repeats.

Every response body is stable, key-sorted JSON produced by
:mod:`accountsvc.jsonutil`.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import http.server
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional

from . import jsonutil
from .errors import (
    AccountSvcError,
    AuthenticationError,
    AuthorizationError,
    ConflictError,
    NotFoundError,
    ValidationError,
)
from .recovery import RecoveryService
from .repository import Repository

_STATUS_FOR_ERROR = {
    NotFoundError: 404,
    ValidationError: 400,
    ConflictError: 409,
    AuthenticationError: 401,
    AuthorizationError: 403,
}


def _status_for(exc: AccountSvcError) -> int:
    for exc_type, status in _STATUS_FOR_ERROR.items():
        if isinstance(exc, exc_type):
            return status
    return 400


def _account_view(repository: Repository, account_id: str) -> dict:
    account = repository.get_account(account_id)
    return {
        "account_id": account["account_id"],
        "org_id": account["org_id"],
        "current_email": account["current_email"],
        "status": account["status"],
        "created_at": account["created_at"],
        "recovered_at": account["recovered_at"],
        "email_history": repository.email_history_for_account(account_id),
        "mfa_factors": repository.list_mfa_factors(account_id),
    }


def _ticket_view(repository: Repository, ticket_id: str) -> dict:
    return repository.get_ticket(ticket_id)


def _request_view(repository: Repository, request_id: str) -> dict:
    return repository.get_recovery_request_view(request_id)


_DISALLOWED_STAGING_FIELDS = (
    "account_id",
    "email",
    "email_at_request",
    "recipient",
    "address",
    "token",
    "token_plaintext",
    "token_hash",
)


def _reject_disallowed_staging_fields(body: dict) -> None:
    present = [key for key in _DISALLOWED_STAGING_FIELDS if key in body]
    if present:
        raise ValidationError(
            "retry staging must not include caller-supplied "
            + ", ".join(present)
        )


def make_handler(
    repository: Repository,
    recovery_service: RecoveryService,
    bearer_token: str,
) -> type[http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler]:
    def require_auth(headers) -> None:
        header = headers.get("Authorization", "")
        prefix = "Bearer "
        supplied = header[len(prefix):] if header.startswith(prefix) else ""
        if not supplied or not hmac.compare_digest(supplied, bearer_token):
            raise AuthenticationError("a valid bearer token is required")

    class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        server_version = "accountsvc/0.1"

        def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # noqa: A002
            pass  # keep test/CLI output quiet; failures still surface via responses

        def _send_json(self, status: int, payload: dict) -> None:
            body = jsonutil.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8")
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

        def _read_json(self) -> dict:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0") or "0")
            if length == 0:
                return {}
            raw = self.rfile.read(length)
            try:
                data = jsonutil.loads(raw)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise ValidationError(f"request body is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
            if not isinstance(data, dict):
                raise ValidationError("request body must be a JSON object")
            return data

        def _dispatch(self, routes: list[tuple[str, Callable[[], None]]]) -> None:
            path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0].rstrip("/") or "/"
            for route_path, handler in routes:
                if route_path == path:
                    try:
                        handler()
                    except AccountSvcError as exc:
                        self._send_json(_status_for(exc), {"error": str(exc)})
                    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                        self._send_json(500, {"error": f"internal error: {exc}"})
                    return
            self._send_json(404, {"error": f"no route for {self.command} {path}"})

        # -- unauthenticated recovery flow -------------------------------

        def _handle_recovery_start(self) -> None:
            body = self._read_json()
            org_id = _require_str(body, "organization")
            email = _require_str(body, "email")
            result = recovery_service.start(org_id, email)
            self._send_json(202, result)

        def _handle_recovery_complete(self) -> None:
            body = self._read_json()
            token = _require_str(body, "token")
            result = recovery_service.complete(token)
            self._send_json(200, result)

        # -- authenticated administration ---------------------------------

        def _handle_notifications_retry(self) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            body = self._read_json()
            request_id = body.get("request_id")
            result = recovery_service.retry_notifications(request_id)
            self._send_json(200, result)

        def _handle_admin_get_account(self, account_id: str) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            self._send_json(200, _account_view(repository, account_id))

        def _handle_admin_get_ticket(self, ticket_id: str) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            self._send_json(200, _ticket_view(repository, ticket_id))

        def _handle_admin_get_request(self, request_id: str) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            self._send_json(200, _request_view(repository, request_id))

        def _handle_admin_create_ticket(self) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            body = self._read_json()
            ticket = repository.create_ticket(
                linked_request_id=_require_str(body, "linked_request_id"),
                subject=_require_str(body, "subject"),
                operator_id=_require_str(body, "operator_id"),
            )
            self._send_json(201, ticket)

        def _handle_admin_create_operator(self) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            body = self._read_json()
            operator = repository.create_operator(_require_str(body, "display_name"))
            self._send_json(201, operator)

        def _handle_admin_assign_operator_role(self) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            body = self._read_json()
            assignment = repository.assign_operator_role(
                operator_id=_require_str(body, "operator_id"),
                org_id=_require_str(body, "organization"),
                role=_require_str(body, "role"),
            )
            self._send_json(200, assignment)

        def _handle_admin_revoke_operator_role(self) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            body = self._read_json()
            assignment = repository.revoke_operator_role(
                operator_id=_require_str(body, "operator_id"),
                org_id=_require_str(body, "organization"),
            )
            self._send_json(200, assignment)

        def _handle_admin_stage_retry(self) -> None:
            require_auth(self.headers)
            body = self._read_json()
            _reject_disallowed_staging_fields(body)
            staging = recovery_service.stage_single_retry(
                request_id=_require_str(body, "request_id"),
                operator_id=_require_str(body, "operator_id"),
            )
            self._send_json(201, staging)

        def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
            path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0].rstrip("/") or "/"
            if path == "/admin/tickets":
                self._dispatch([(path, self._handle_admin_create_ticket)])
                return
            if path == "/admin/operators":
                self._dispatch([(path, self._handle_admin_create_operator)])
                return
            if path == "/admin/operator-roles":
                self._dispatch([(path, self._handle_admin_assign_operator_role)])
                return
            if path == "/admin/operator-roles/revoke":
                self._dispatch([(path, self._handle_admin_revoke_operator_role)])
                return
            if path == "/admin/retry-stagings":
                self._dispatch([(path, self._handle_admin_stage_retry)])
                return
            self._dispatch(
                [
                    ("/recovery/start", self._handle_recovery_start),
                    ("/recovery/complete", self._handle_recovery_complete),
                    (
                        "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                        self._handle_notifications_retry,
                    ),
                ]
            )

        def do_GET(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
            path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0].rstrip("/") or "/"
            parts = [p for p in path.split("/") if p]
            if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "admin" and parts[1] == "accounts":
                account_id = parts[2]
                self._dispatch(
                    [(path, lambda: self._handle_admin_get_account(account_id))]
                )
                return
            if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "admin" and parts[1] == "tickets":
                ticket_id = parts[2]
                self._dispatch(
                    [(path, lambda: self._handle_admin_get_ticket(ticket_id))]
                )
                return
            if len(parts) == 3 and parts[0] == "admin" and parts[1] == "requests":
                request_id = parts[2]
                self._dispatch(
                    [(path, lambda: self._handle_admin_get_request(request_id))]
                )
                return
            self._send_json(404, {"error": f"no route for GET {path}"})

    return Handler


def _require_str(body: dict, key: str) -> str:
    value = body.get(key)
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        raise ValidationError(f"{key!r} is required")
    return value


class LoopbackHTTPServer(http.server.HTTPServer):
    """Single-threaded on purpose: requests share one sqlite connection and
    are handled one at a time, so no additional locking is needed.
    """

    allow_reuse_address = True


def build_server(
    repository: Repository,
    recovery_service: RecoveryService,
    bearer_token: str,
    host: str = "127.0.0.1",
    port: int = 0,
) -> LoopbackHTTPServer:
    handler_cls = make_handler(repository, recovery_service, bearer_token)
    return LoopbackHTTPServer((host, port), handler_cls)
