class OperatorRetryAcrossRestartsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """One end-to-end integration test covering the retry-notification
    consumer from every angle that matters for durability and correctness:
    an operator-staged notice surviving a real process restart, ordinary
    failed notices retried both before and after their token expires, an
    opaque failing provider response that names the wrong account, and a
    staged notice whose target account changes address before the restart
    that finally delivers it. Every recovery token used in assertions is
    captured from what was actually POSTed to the fake mail provider --
    never from an admin surface, since the service must never expose a
    recovery token there.
    """

    RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = "60"

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.bearer_token = "s3cret-operator-retry-token"
        self.mail_state = _ScriptedMailState()
        mail_port = _free_port()
        self.mail_server = http.server.HTTPServer(
            ("127.0.0.1", mail_port), _make_scripted_mail_handler(self.mail_state)
        )
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self.mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True
        )
        self.mail_thread.start()
        self.mail_endpoint = f"http://127.0.0.1:{mail_port}/"

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.mail_server.shutdown()
        self.mail_thread.join(timeout=5)
        self.mail_server.server_close()
        self.tmpdir.cleanup()

    def _db(self, name: str) -> str:
        return str(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / name)

    def _start(self, database: str, *extra_args: str) -> tuple[subprocess.Popen, str]:
        return start_serve_process(
            database,
            self.bearer_token,
            self.mail_endpoint,
            "--recovery-token-ttl-seconds",
            self.RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
            *extra_args,
        )

    def test_operator_retry_uses_current_address_after_restart(self) -> None:
        self._verify_shared_route_calls_account_service_retry_notifications()
        self._phase_operator_staged_retry_survives_restart()
        self._phase_fresh_and_expired_ordinary_retries()
        self._phase_decoy_locator_is_ignored()
        self._phase_email_change_before_restart()

    # -- wiring: the shared consumer route must call AccountService.retry_notifications --

    def _verify_shared_route_calls_account_service_retry_notifications(self) -> None:
        conn = db.connect(":memory:")
        repo = Repository(conn)
        repo.create_organization("ORG_WIRING")
        repo.create_account("ORG_WIRING", "ACC_WIRING", "wiring@example.test")
        mailer = MailClient(self.mail_endpoint)
        recovery_service = AccountService(repo, mailer)
        server = build_server(repo, recovery_service, self.bearer_token, port=0)
        base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}"
        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        try:
            with mock.patch.object(
                recovery_service,
                "retry_notifications",
                wraps=recovery_service.retry_notifications,
            ) as spy:
                status, body = _http_json(
                    "POST",
                    base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                    {},
                    bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
                )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(body, {"retried": []})
            spy.assert_called_once_with()
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            thread.join(timeout=5)
            server.server_close()
            conn.close()

    # -- one scoped operator, one open ticket, one failed notice, staged then restarted --

    def _phase_operator_staged_retry_survives_restart(self) -> None:
        database = self._db("phase1.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_P1", "--database", database)
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P1", "ACC_P1", "person1@example.test",
            "--database", database,
        )
        code, out, err = run_cli("create-operator", "Ada Support", "--database", database)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        operator_id = json.loads(out)["operator_id"]
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "assign-operator-role", operator_id, "ORG_P1", "agent", "--database", database
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)

        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"provider-down")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/start",
                {"organization": "ORG_P1", "email": "person1@example.test"},
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
            request_id = body["request_id"]
            original_token = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]

            status, ticket = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/admin/tickets",
                {
                    "linked_request_id": request_id,
                    "operator_id": operator_id,
                    "subject": "Locked out",
                },
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 201, ticket)

            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, staging = _http_json(
                "POST",
                f"{base_url}/recovery/requests/{request_id}/retry",
                {"operator_id": operator_id},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 201, staging)
            self.assertEqual(staging["result"], "reserved")
            # The request route only stages; it must never send mail itself.
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

        # A fresh service process, over the same durable database, is what
        # actually delivers the reservation the first process staged.
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(
                [entry["staging_id"] for entry in body["retried"]],
                [staging["staging_id"]],
            )
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "sent")
            new_calls = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            self.assertEqual(new_calls, [("person1@example.test", original_token)])
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    # -- ordinary (non-staged) notices: one still fresh, one past its ttl --

    def _create_ordinary_failed_notice(
        self, database: str, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str
    ) -> str:
        run_cli("create-org", org_id, "--database", database)
        run_cli("create-account", org_id, account_id, email, "--database", database)

        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"provider-down")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database, "--clock-now", "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z")
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/start", {"organization": org_id, "email": email}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
            return self.mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    def _phase_fresh_and_expired_ordinary_retries(self) -> None:
        fresh_database = self._db("phase2_fresh.db")
        expired_database = self._db("phase2_expired.db")
        fresh_token = self._create_ordinary_failed_notice(
            fresh_database, "ORG_P2F", "ACC_P2F", "fresh@example.test"
        )
        expired_token = self._create_ordinary_failed_notice(
            expired_database, "ORG_P2E", "ACC_P2E", "expired@example.test"
        )

        # Still within the 60s ttl: the retry must deliver.
        proc, base_url = self._start(fresh_database, "--clock-now", "2030-01-01T00:00:30Z")
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(len(body["retried"]), 1)
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "sent")
            new_calls = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            self.assertEqual(new_calls, [("fresh@example.test", fresh_token)])
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

        # Past the 60s ttl: the retry must not reach the mailer at all, and
        # the token it recorded must no longer complete recovery.
        proc, base_url = self._start(expired_database, "--clock-now", "2030-01-01T00:01:01Z")
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"], [])
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)

            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/complete", {"token": expired_token}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 400, body)
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    # -- an opaque failing receipt naming a decoy account must be ignored --

    def _phase_decoy_locator_is_ignored(self) -> None:
        database = self._db("phase3.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_P3", "--database", database)
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P3", "ACCOUNT_TRUSTED", "trusted@example.test",
            "--database", database,
        )
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P3", "ACCOUNT_DECOY", "decoy@example.test",
            "--database", database,
        )

        # No separator, no structure -- just the bare id of an unrelated
        # account, to prove the starter resolver never parses the receipt.
        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"ACCOUNT_DECOY")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/start",
                {"organization": "ORG_P3", "email": "trusted@example.test"},
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
            original_token = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]

            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(len(body["retried"]), 1)
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "sent")
            new_calls = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            self.assertEqual(new_calls, [("trusted@example.test", original_token)])
            self.assertNotIn(
                "decoy@example.test",
                [recipient for recipient, _token in self.mail_state.calls],
            )

            # A caller-supplied selector must be rejected outright, before
            # ever reaching the mailer -- the decoy account included.
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                {"account_id": "ACCOUNT_DECOY"},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 400, body)
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)

            status, _body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 401)
            status, _body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token="wrong-token",
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 401)
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    # -- a staged notice whose account changes address before the restart --

    def _phase_email_change_before_restart(self) -> None:
        database = self._db("phase4.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_P4", "--database", database)
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P4", "ACC_P4", "before@example.test",
            "--database", database,
        )
        code, out, err = run_cli("create-operator", "Ada Support", "--database", database)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        operator_id = json.loads(out)["operator_id"]
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "assign-operator-role", operator_id, "ORG_P4", "agent", "--database", database
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)

        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"provider-down")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)

class OperatorRetryAcrossRestartsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """One end-to-end integration test covering the retry-notification
    consumer from every angle that matters for durability and correctness:
    an operator-staged notice surviving a real process restart, ordinary
    failed notices retried both before and after their token expires, an
    opaque failing provider response that names the wrong account, and a
    staged notice whose target account changes address before the restart
    that finally delivers it. Every recovery token used in assertions is
    captured from what was actually POSTed to the fake mail provider --
    never from an admin surface, since the service must never expose a
    recovery token there.
    """

    RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = "60"

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.bearer_token = "s3cret-operator-retry-token"
        self.mail_state = _ScriptedMailState()
        mail_port = _free_port()
        self.mail_server = http.server.HTTPServer(
            ("127.0.0.1", mail_port), _make_scripted_mail_handler(self.mail_state)
        )
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self.mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True
        )
        self.mail_thread.start()
        self.mail_endpoint = f"http://127.0.0.1:{mail_port}/"

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.mail_server.shutdown()
        self.mail_thread.join(timeout=5)
        self.mail_server.server_close()
        self.tmpdir.cleanup()

    def _db(self, name: str) -> str:
        return str(Path(self.tmpdir.name) / name)

    def _start(self, database: str, *extra_args: str) -> tuple[subprocess.Popen, str]:
        return start_serve_process(
            database,
            self.bearer_token,
            self.mail_endpoint,
            "--recovery-token-ttl-seconds",
            self.RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
            *extra_args,
        )

    def test_operator_retry_uses_current_address_after_restart(self) -> None:
        self._verify_shared_route_calls_account_service_retry_notifications()
        self._phase_operator_staged_retry_survives_restart()
        self._phase_fresh_and_expired_ordinary_retries()
        self._phase_decoy_locator_is_ignored()
        self._phase_email_change_before_restart()

    # -- wiring: the shared consumer route must call AccountService.retry_notifications --

    def _verify_shared_route_calls_account_service_retry_notifications(self) -> None:
        conn = db.connect(":memory:")
        repo = Repository(conn)
        repo.create_organization("ORG_WIRING")
        repo.create_account("ORG_WIRING", "ACC_WIRING", "wiring@example.test")
        mailer = MailClient(self.mail_endpoint)
        recovery_service = AccountService(repo, mailer)
        server = build_server(repo, recovery_service, self.bearer_token, port=0)
        base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{server.server_address[1]}"
        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        thread.start()
        try:
            with mock.patch.object(
                recovery_service,
                "retry_notifications",
                wraps=recovery_service.retry_notifications,
            ) as spy:
                status, body = _http_json(
                    "POST",
                    base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                    {},
                    bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
                )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(body, {"retried": []})
            spy.assert_called_once_with()
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            thread.join(timeout=5)
            server.server_close()
            conn.close()

    # -- one scoped operator, one open ticket, one failed notice, staged then restarted --

    def _phase_operator_staged_retry_survives_restart(self) -> None:
        database = self._db("phase1.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_P1", "--database", database)
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P1", "ACC_P1", "person1@example.test",
            "--database", database,
        )
        code, out, err = run_cli("create-operator", "Ada Support", "--database", database)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        operator_id = json.loads(out)["operator_id"]
        code, out, err = run_cli(
            "assign-operator-role", operator_id, "ORG_P1", "agent", "--database", database
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)

        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"provider-down")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/start",
                {"organization": "ORG_P1", "email": "person1@example.test"},
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
            request_id = body["request_id"]
            original_token = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]

            status, ticket = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/admin/tickets",
                {
                    "linked_request_id": request_id,
                    "operator_id": operator_id,
                    "subject": "Locked out",
                },
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 201, ticket)

            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, staging = _http_json(
                "POST",
                f"{base_url}/recovery/requests/{request_id}/retry",
                {"operator_id": operator_id},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 201, staging)
            self.assertEqual(staging["result"], "reserved")
            # The request route only stages; it must never send mail itself.
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

        # A fresh service process, over the same durable database, is what
        # actually delivers the reservation the first process staged.
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(
                [entry["staging_id"] for entry in body["retried"]],
                [staging["staging_id"]],
            )
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "sent")
            new_calls = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            self.assertEqual(new_calls, [("person1@example.test", original_token)])
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    # -- ordinary (non-staged) notices: one still fresh, one past its ttl --

    def _create_ordinary_failed_notice(
        self, database: str, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str
    ) -> str:
        run_cli("create-org", org_id, "--database", database)
        run_cli("create-account", org_id, account_id, email, "--database", database)

        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"provider-down")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database, "--clock-now", "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z")
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/start", {"organization": org_id, "email": email}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
            return self.mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    def _phase_fresh_and_expired_ordinary_retries(self) -> None:
        fresh_database = self._db("phase2_fresh.db")
        expired_database = self._db("phase2_expired.db")
        fresh_token = self._create_ordinary_failed_notice(
            fresh_database, "ORG_P2F", "ACC_P2F", "fresh@example.test"
        )
        expired_token = self._create_ordinary_failed_notice(
            expired_database, "ORG_P2E", "ACC_P2E", "expired@example.test"
        )

        # Still within the 60s ttl: the retry must deliver.
        proc, base_url = self._start(fresh_database, "--clock-now", "2030-01-01T00:00:30Z")
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(len(body["retried"]), 1)
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "sent")
            new_calls = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            self.assertEqual(new_calls, [("fresh@example.test", fresh_token)])
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

        # Past the 60s ttl: the retry must not reach the mailer at all, and
        # the token it recorded must no longer complete recovery.
        proc, base_url = self._start(expired_database, "--clock-now", "2030-01-01T00:01:01Z")
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"], [])
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)

            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/complete", {"token": expired_token}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 400, body)
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

    # -- an opaque failing receipt naming a decoy account must be ignored --

    def _phase_decoy_locator_is_ignored(self) -> None:
        database = self._db("phase3.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_P3", "--database", database)
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P3", "ACCOUNT_TRUSTED", "trusted@example.test",

        )
        run_cli(
            "create-account", "ORG_P3", "ACCOUNT_DECOY", "decoy@example.test",
            "--database", database,
        )

        # No separator, no structure -- just the bare id of an unrelated
        # account, to prove the starter resolver never parses the receipt.
        self.mail_state.push_failure(b"ACCOUNT_DECOY")
        proc, base_url = self._start(database)
        try:
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/start",
                {"organization": "ORG_P3", "email": "trusted@example.test"},
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 202, body)
            self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "queued_for_retry")
            original_token = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]

            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
            self.assertEqual(len(body["retried"]), 1)
            self.assertEqual(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"], "sent")
            new_calls = self.mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            self.assertEqual(new_calls, [("trusted@example.test", original_token)])
            self.assertNotIn(
                "decoy@example.test",
                [recipient for recipient, _token in self.mail_state.calls],

            # A caller-supplied selector must be rejected outright, before
            # ever reaching the mailer -- the decoy account included.
            calls_before = len(self.mail_state.calls)
            status, body = _http_json(
                "POST",
                base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry",
                {"account_id": "ACCOUNT_DECOY"},
                bearer_token=self.bearer_token,
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 400, body)
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)

            status, _body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {}
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 401)
            status, _body = _http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token="wrong-token",
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 401)
            self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_state.calls), calls_before)
        finally:
            stop_serve_process(proc)

def retry_notifications(self) -> dict:
        """Redeliver every eligible failed or operator-staged recovery
        notification, reloading all of it fresh from durable SQLite storage.

        Nothing here is tracked in memory between calls, so this is safe to
        run repeatedly, and safe to run in a different process (e.g. after
        the server that recorded a failure or staged a retry has restarted)
        from whatever process originally created that state. An ordinary
        failed notice, like an operator-staged one, is re-checked for
        expiry immediately before redelivery and, if expired, is durably
        marked so and never handed to the mailer. An operator-staged notice
        is re-validated further still -- authorization and request status
        can also have changed since it was staged -- and skipped (with its
        reservation finalized to a terminal, non-'reserved' result so it is
        never retried again) rather than delivered, if it is no longer
        eligible.
        """

        retried = []
        for request in self._repository.requests_needing_retry():
            if is_expired(request["expires_at"]):
                self._repository.expire_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
                continue
            retried.append(self._retry_reloaded_notice(request))
        for staging in self._repository.list_reserved_retry_stagings():
            request, _skipped = self._repository.prepare_staged_notice_for_retry(
                staging["staging_id"]
            )
            if request is None:
                continue

"""Recovery request lifecycle: start, complete, and notification retry.

The account bound to a recovery request is fixed at creation time
(``request["account_id"]``). Every later step in this module -- delivery,
retry, and completion -- uses that stored binding. Nothing here re-derives
the account from current email ownership, so a later email change (or an
address being claimed by a different account) never redirects an
outstanding request.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from . import idgen, notice
from .errors import NotFoundError, ValidationError
from .mailer import MailClient
from .repository import Repository
from .timeutil import is_expired

DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS = 30 * 60
DEFAULT_STAGING_RATE_LIMIT = 5
DEFAULT_STAGING_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS = 60


class RecoveryService:
    def __init__(
        self,
        repository: Repository,
        mailer: MailClient,
        ttl_seconds: int = DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS,
        staging_rate_limit: int = DEFAULT_STAGING_RATE_LIMIT,
        staging_rate_limit_window_seconds: int = DEFAULT_STAGING_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS,
    ):
        self._repository = repository
        self._mailer = mailer
        self._ttl_seconds = ttl_seconds
        self._staging_rate_limit = staging_rate_limit
        self._staging_rate_limit_window_seconds = staging_rate_limit_window_seconds

    def start(self, org_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
        account = self._repository.find_account_by_current_email(org_id, email)
        if account is None:
            raise NotFoundError(
                f"no account in organization {org_id!r} currently uses email {email!r}"
            )
        token = idgen.new_secret_token()
        request = self._repository.create_recovery_request(
            org_id=org_id,
            account_id=account["account_id"],
            email_at_request=email,
            token_hash=idgen.hash_token(token),
            token_plaintext=token,
            ttl_seconds=self._ttl_seconds,
        )
        delivery_status = self._deliver(
            request, token, account["account_id"], account["current_email"]
        )
        return {
            "request_id": request["request_id"],
            "delivery_status": delivery_status,
        }

    def _deliver(self, request: dict, token: str, account_id: str, recipient: str) -> str:
        """Send ``token`` through the mail path to ``recipient``.

        ``recipient`` is always the resolved account's *current* trusted
        address, supplied by the caller -- never the request's frozen
        ``email_at_request``, which can end up owned by a different account
        after an email change and so must never be (re)used as a delivery
        target.
        """

        result = self._mailer.send_recovery_notification(recipient, token)
        if result.success:
            self._repository.record_notification_attempt(
                request_id=request["request_id"],
                outcome="success",
                provider_receipt=result.receipt,
                retry_locator=None,
                error_detail=None,
            )
            return "sent"
        locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(result.receipt, account_id)
        self._repository.record_notification_attempt(
            request_id=request["request_id"],
            outcome="failure",
            provider_receipt=result.receipt,
            retry_locator=locator,
            error_detail=result.error,
        )
        return "queued_for_retry"

    def complete(self, token: str) -> dict:
        token_hash = idgen.hash_token(token)
        request = self._repository.find_recovery_request_by_token_hash(token_hash)
        if request is None:
            raise ValidationError("recovery token is invalid")
        if request["status"] == "completed":
            raise ValidationError("recovery token has already been used")
        if request["status"] != "pending":
            raise ValidationError(f"recovery token is {request['status']}")
        if is_expired(request["expires_at"]):
            self._repository.expire_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
            raise ValidationError("recovery token has expired")

        self._repository.complete_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
        self._repository.mark_account_recovered(request["account_id"])
        return {
            "request_id": request["request_id"],
            "account_id": request["account_id"],
            "organization": request["org_id"],
            "status": "completed",
        }

    def stage_single_retry(self, request_id: str, operator_id: str) -> dict:
        """Authorize and durably reserve a retry for exactly one request.

        The operator selects only ``request_id``; the ticket and
        organization are derived from that request's open linked ticket and
        the operator's role there is required to be active. Ticket
        authorization and recovery-token validation are checked as two
        separate steps, and -- together with a per-operator rate limit --
        are enforced atomically in one reservation, so a rejected attempt
        never gets an audit record. Staging never sends mail itself: the
        reservation is handed back as-is, and actual redelivery happens
        later when :meth:`retry_notifications` reloads it from durable
        storage -- in this process or, after a restart, a different one.
        Repeated staging within the rate limit simply produces another
        independent reservation rather than being deduplicated.
        """

        _ticket, _request, staging = self._repository.reserve_staging_for_retry(
            request_id,
            operator_id,
            self._staging_rate_limit,
            self._staging_rate_limit_window_seconds,
        )
        return staging

    def retry_notifications(self) -> dict:
        """Redeliver every eligible failed or operator-staged recovery
        notification, reloading all of it fresh from durable SQLite storage.

        Nothing here is tracked in memory between calls, so this is safe to
        run repeatedly, and safe to run in a different process (e.g. after
        the server that recorded a failure or staged a retry has restarted)
        from whatever process originally created that state. An ordinary
        failed notice, like an operator-staged one, is re-checked for
        expiry immediately before redelivery and, if expired, is durably
        marked so and never handed to the mailer. An operator-staged notice
        is re-validated further still -- authorization and request status
        can also have changed since it was staged -- and skipped (with its
        reservation finalized to a terminal, non-'reserved' result so it is
        never retried again) rather than delivered, if it is no longer
        eligible.
        """

        retried = []
        for request in self._repository.requests_needing_retry():
            if is_expired(request["expires_at"]):
                self._repository.expire_recovery_request(request["request_id"])
                continue
            retried.append(self._retry_reloaded_notice(request))
        for staging in self._repository.list_reserved_retry_stagings():
            request, _skipped = self._repository.prepare_staged_notice_for_retry(
                staging["staging_id"]
            )
            if request is None:
                continue
            outcome = self._retry_reloaded_notice(request)
            self._repository.finalize_retry_staging(
                staging["staging_id"], outcome["delivery_status"]
            )
            outcome["staging_id"] = staging["staging_id"]
            retried.append(outcome)
        return {"retried": retried}

    def _retry_reloaded_notice(self, request: dict) -> dict:
        resolved_account_id, recipient = self._resolve_retry_recipient(request)
        token = request["token_plaintext"]
        delivery_status = self._deliver(request, token, resolved_account_id, recipient)
        return {"request_id": request["request_id"], "delivery_status": delivery_status}

    def _resolve_retry_recipient(self, request: dict) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Resolve the account a retry is bound to, and its *current*
        trusted address to deliver to.

        The account comes from ``notice.account_id_from_retry_locator``,
        the starter resolver, used unmodified: the request's own
        ``account_id`` is always the fallback and, per that resolver's
        contract, always wins over whatever the saved locator contains.
        The recipient is that account's current email looked up fresh --
        never the request's frozen ``email_at_request`` -- since the
        account may have changed its address (or its old address may have
        been claimed by an unrelated account) since the request was first
        created.
        """

        latest = self._repository.latest_notification_attempt(request["request_id"])
        saved_locator = latest["retry_locator"] if latest else None
        resolved_account_id = notice.account_id_from_retry_locator(
            saved_locator, request["account_id"]
        )
        recipient = self._repository.get_account(resolved_account_id)["current_email"]
        return resolved_account_id, recipient


# Public alias: HTTP route wiring and integration tests refer to this
# service by the name AccountService.
AccountService = RecoveryService

# Support operator guide: recovery notification retry

This guide is for support operators and the engineers who administer them.
It covers how to stage a retry for a stuck account-recovery notification,
what the service checks along the way, and how to read the audit trail
afterward. It assumes the loopback HTTP service is already running
(`python -m accountsvc.cli serve ...`) and that you have the shared
administrative bearer token.

## Role scope

Every operator action is authorized against an **organization-scoped
role**, stored in `operator_org_roles` and keyed by `(operator_id,
org_id)`:

- The same operator may hold a role in one organization and no role at all
  in another. Holding an active role in Organization A never authorizes
  any action against a ticket or request that belongs to Organization B.
- A role is either `active` or `revoked`. Revoking an operator's role in
  an organization (`POST /admin/operator-roles/revoke` or
  `revoke-operator-role`) takes effect immediately: any ticket-creation or
  retry-staging attempt from that operator in that organization is
  rejected (`403`) from that point on.
- Reassigning a role (`POST /admin/operator-roles` or
  `assign-operator-role`) reactivates a previously revoked assignment. The
  same call covers initial assignment, a role change, and reinstatement.

There is no cross-organization override and no "super operator" role --
every check is scoped to the one organization a ticket or request belongs
to.

## Ticket linkage

A support ticket exists only to authorize staging a retry for **exactly
one** recovery request:

- `POST /admin/tickets` takes `linked_request_id`, `operator_id`, and
  `subject`. The organization and account for the ticket are derived
  *only* from the linked request -- a ticket row never stores an account
  identifier, an email address, or a recovery token of its own.
- The link is immutable. Nothing in the service ever repoints a ticket at
  a different request after creation.
- Opening a ticket requires the named operator to already hold an active
  role in the linked request's organization (see Role scope above).
- The subject line is validated at creation: it must not contain an `@`
  address, the linked request's account id, or its plaintext recovery
  token. Ticket subjects end up in general-purpose support tooling, so
  they are held to the same no-secrets standard as any other audit
  surface.
- Staging a retry (`POST /recovery/requests/<request_id>/retry`) does not
  take a ticket id at all -- it derives the ticket from the request's
  *open* linked ticket. A closed ticket blocks staging until a new one is
  opened; there is no way to stage through a closed ticket by supplying
  its id directly.

## Authentication

Every route except `POST /recovery/start` and `POST /recovery/complete`
requires an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, checked with a
constant-time comparison against the token the service was started with
(`--bearer-token`). A missing or incorrect token is rejected with `401`
before any other check runs -- including before the request body is
inspected for staging or retry fields. There is no per-operator
authentication token; the operator identity for an action comes from the
`operator_id` in the request body (or the URL path, for ticket-scoped
routes), not from the bearer token itself. Treat the bearer token as an
administrative credential shared by your support tooling, not an
individual operator's login.

## Rate limits

Retry staging is rate-limited per operator to guard against a support
tool (or a person) retrying the same request in a loop:

- The limit is a sliding window: at most `staging_rate_limit` staging
  attempts (default **5**) per operator in the trailing
  `staging_rate_limit_window_seconds` (default **60**), counted against
  `retry_stagings` rows regardless of which request they were for.
- Exceeding the limit responds `429` and the attempt is rejected before it
  is recorded -- a rate-limited attempt leaves no audit row.
- The limit is enforced atomically with ticket authorization and the
  reservation insert, in one database transaction, so it holds even
  against retries issued in quick succession from different processes
  against the same durable database.
- Staging within the limit is otherwise unrestricted: repeatedly staging a
  retry for the *same* request is allowed and simply produces another
  independent reservation, not an error.

If a support workflow is legitimately hitting the default limit (bulk
recovery incidents, for example), raise `staging_rate_limit` /
`staging_rate_limit_window_seconds` when constructing the service rather
than working around the limit per call.

## Audit fields

Every retry-staging attempt that passes authorization is recorded in
`retry_stagings`, whether or not it is ever delivered, and whether or not
it is a repeat of an earlier attempt for the same request:

| Column        | Meaning                                                        |
|---------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `staging_id`  | Opaque id of this reservation.                                  |
| `operator_id` | The operator who staged the retry.                              |
| `org_id`      | The organization, derived from the linked ticket.                |
| `ticket_id`   | The open ticket the retry was staged through.                    |
| `request_id`  | The recovery request being retried.                              |
| `result`      | `reserved` until delivery is attempted; see below for terminal values. |
| `created_at`  | When the reservation was recorded.                               |

**The recovery token is never a column here, and is never included in any
response that returns this row.** The staging record proves *who staged a
retry for which request, when, and with what outcome* -- it never carries
anything that would let a reader of the audit trail redeem the recovery
token themselves.

`result` starts as `reserved` (staging never sends mail itself) and is
finalized to exactly one of:

- `sent` / `queued_for_retry` -- the consumer (`POST
  /recovery/notifications/retry`) attempted delivery and recorded the
  mail provider's outcome.
- `skipped_unauthorized` -- by the time the consumer ran, the ticket had
  closed or the operator's role was no longer active.
- `skipped_completed` -- the underlying recovery request was completed
  (the end user redeemed it another way) before the consumer ran.
- `skipped_expired` -- the recovery token expired before the consumer ran;
  the request is also durably marked `expired` at this point.

A `reserved` row that never advances usually means the consumer has not
run since it was staged -- see the next section.

## Staging vs. delivery

Staging (`POST /recovery/requests/<request_id>/retry`) and delivery
(`POST /recovery/notifications/retry`) are deliberately two different
calls:

1. Staging authorizes the operator, validates the recovery token is still
   live, enforces the rate limit, and records a `reserved` row. **It never
   sends mail.** This keeps staging fast and side-effect-free even if the
   mail provider is slow or down.
2. The consumer reloads every eligible notice -- both `reserved`
   operator-staged ones and ordinary failed ones from `POST
   /recovery/start` -- fresh from durable storage and attempts delivery
   for each. It always delivers to the target account's *current* email
   address, never the address recorded on the original request, since
   that address may since have been claimed by a different account.

Because the consumer reloads everything from the database rather than
tracking anything in memory, it is safe to run it from a different process
than whichever one did the staging -- including after a full service
restart. There is nothing else to "wire up" operationally: call the
consumer route on whatever process is currently running.

## Operational flags

`serve` accepts `--recovery-token-ttl-seconds` (how long a newly created
recovery token stays valid) and `--clock-now` (freeze the server's clock
at a fixed UTC timestamp instead of the real one). Both exist primarily
for deterministic testing; day-to-day operation should omit `--clock-now`
and let the service use the real clock.

# Release notes

## Recovery notification retry: staged delivery, rate limits, and audit hardening

This iteration reworks how a stuck recovery notification gets resent,
splitting "an operator authorizes a retry" from "the service actually
sends mail" into two separate, durable steps, and closes several gaps in
the retry path along the way.

### Staging and delivery are now separate

- `POST /recovery/requests/<request_id>/retry` (replacing the old
  `POST /admin/retry-stagings`) authorizes an operator against the
  request's open linked ticket and reserves a retry. **It never sends
  mail.** Ticket authorization, recovery-token validity, and a
  per-operator rate limit are all enforced atomically before the
  reservation is recorded, so a rejected attempt leaves no audit row.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` is now the single consumer that
  actually delivers: it reloads every eligible notice -- ordinary failed
  ones and reserved operator-staged ones alike -- fresh from durable
  SQLite storage and attempts delivery for each. It accepts no request
  fields; a non-empty body (including a caller-supplied `request_id` or
  `account_id`) is rejected with `400`, since it always processes every
  eligible notice rather than a caller-chosen subset.
- Because the consumer reloads all of its state from storage, it is safe
  to run in a different process than whichever one did the staging --
  including after the service has restarted.

### Retries now always target the current address

Every retry -- ordinary or operator-staged -- delivers to the target
account's *current* email address, looked up fresh at retry time, never
the frozen `email_at_request` recorded on the original request. An
account's original address can later be released and claimed by a
different account; resending to the frozen address would risk delivering
the recovery token to that new owner instead. The account itself is still
resolved through `accountsvc.notice.account_id_from_retry_locator`, the
starter resolver, unmodified -- only the delivery address changed.

### Two correctness fixes in the consumer

- Ordinary (non-staged) failed notices are now re-checked for expiry
  immediately before redelivery, the same way operator-staged notices
  already were. Previously an ordinary notice past its token's expiry
  could still be handed to the mail provider.
- A request that has a reserved operator staging is retried only through
  that staging, even though it can simultaneously match the ordinary
  failed-notice query. Previously such a request could be delivered to
  twice in a single consumer run.

A staged reservation that is no longer eligible by the time the consumer
runs -- because its ticket closed, the operator's role was revoked, the
request was completed some other way, or the token expired -- is skipped
and finalized to a terminal, non-`reserved` result
(`skipped_unauthorized`, `skipped_completed`, or `skipped_expired`)
instead of being retried indefinitely.

### Hardening carried in this line of work

- Per-operator rate limiting on retry staging (default 5 per 60s), `429`
  on exceeding it.

# Release notes

## Recovery notification retry: staged delivery, rate limits, and audit hardening

This iteration reworks how a stuck recovery notification gets resent,
splitting "an operator authorizes a retry" from "the service actually
sends mail" into two separate, durable steps, and closes several gaps in
the retry path along the way.

### Staging and delivery are now separate

- `POST /recovery/requests/<request_id>/retry` (replacing the old
  `POST /admin/retry-stagings`) authorizes an operator against the
  request's open linked ticket and reserves a retry. **It never sends
  mail.** Ticket authorization, recovery-token validity, and a
  per-operator rate limit are all enforced atomically before the
  reservation is recorded, so a rejected attempt leaves no audit row.
- `POST /recovery/notifications/retry` is now the single consumer that
  actually delivers: it reloads every eligible notice -- ordinary failed
  ones and reserved operator-staged ones alike -- fresh from durable
  SQLite storage and attempts delivery for each. It accepts no request
  fields; a non-empty body (including a caller-supplied `request_id` or
  `account_id`) is rejected with `400`, since it always processes every
  eligible notice rather than a caller-chosen subset.
- Because the consumer reloads all of its state from storage, it is safe
  to run in a different process than whichever one did the staging --
  including after the service has restarted.

### Retries now always target the current address

Every retry -- ordinary or operator-staged -- delivers to the target
account's *current* email address, looked up fresh at retry time, never
the frozen `email_at_request` recorded on the original request. An
account's original address can later be released and claimed by a
different account; resending to the frozen address would risk delivering
the recovery token to that new owner instead. The account itself is still
resolved through `accountsvc.notice.account_id_from_retry_locator`, the
starter resolver, unmodified -- only the delivery address changed.

### Two correctness fixes in the consumer

- Ordinary (non-staged) failed notices are now re-checked for expiry
  immediately before redelivery, the same way operator-staged notices
  already were. Previously an ordinary notice past its token's expiry
  could still be handed to the mail provider.
- A request that has a reserved operator staging is retried only through
  that staging, even though it can simultaneously match the ordinary
  failed-notice query. Previously such a request could be delivered to
  twice in a single consumer run.

A staged reservation that is no longer eligible by the time the consumer
runs -- because its ticket closed, the operator's role was revoked, the
request was completed some other way, or the token expired -- is skipped
and finalized to a terminal, non-`reserved` result
(`skipped_unauthorized`, `skipped_completed`, or `skipped_expired`)
instead of being retried indefinitely.

### Hardening carried in this line of work

- Per-operator rate limiting on retry staging (default 5 per 60s), `429`
  on exceeding it.
- Every HTTP request body is capped at a fixed byte limit, rejected with
  `400` before being read into memory.
- Ticket authorization and recovery-token validation are two separate
  checks in the repository layer, so an operator can be fully authorized
  on a ticket whose underlying token has independently expired.
- Every administrative and support route requires the shared bearer
  token; `POST /recovery/start` and `POST /recovery/complete` remain the
  only unauthenticated routes.
- Audit records for a staged retry (`retry_stagings`) never contain the
  recovery token, in either the stored row or any response that returns
  it.

### Operational additions

- `serve` accepts `--recovery-token-ttl-seconds` and `--clock-now` (freeze
  the server's clock at a fixed UTC timestamp), primarily for
  deterministic testing.
- `RecoveryService` is now also exported as `AccountService`, the name the
  retry-notification consumer route and its integration tests refer to it
  by.

See `docs/support-operator-guide.md` for the operator-facing runbook and
`README.md` for the full implementation notes.

"""Ad hoc smoke test run live against real subprocesses. Scratch file, not
part of the test suite -- deleted after the manual verification it exists
for.
"""
import http.server
import json
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)


def free_port():
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
    port = s.getsockname()[1]
    s.close()
    return port


class ScriptedMailState:
    def __init__(self):
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
        self.script = []
        self.calls = []

    def push_failure(self, body=b"provider-down", status=502):
        with self.lock:
            self.script.append((status, body))

    def next_response(self):
        with self.lock:
            if self.script:
                return self.script.pop(0)
            return (200, b"ok")

    def record(self, recipient, token):
        with self.lock:
            self.calls.append((recipient, token))


def make_handler(state):
    class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
        def log_message(self, fmt, *args):
            pass

        def do_POST(self):
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0") or "0")
            payload = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length).decode("utf-8"))
            state.record(payload["recipient"], payload["recovery_token"])
            status, body = state.next_response()
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(body)

    return Handler


def wait_for_server(base_url, timeout=5.0):
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            urllib.request.urlopen(base_url + "/recovery/complete", timeout=0.5).close()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            exc.close()
            return
        except (urllib.error.URLError, ConnectionError, OSError):
            time.sleep(0.1)
    raise AssertionError(f"server at {base_url} never became reachable")


def http_json(method, url, body=None, bearer_token=None):
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
    req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    if bearer_token is not None:
        req.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {bearer_token}")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        with exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read().decode("utf-8"))


def run_cli(*args):
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", *args],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        raise AssertionError(f"CLI {args} failed: {proc.stderr}")
    return proc.stdout.strip()


def start_server(database, bearer_token, mail_endpoint, *extra):
    port = free_port()
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [
            sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", "serve",
            "--database", database,
            "--bearer-token", bearer_token,
            "--mail-endpoint", mail_endpoint,
            "--host", "127.0.0.1",
            "--port", str(port),
            "--recovery-token-ttl-seconds", "60",
            *extra,
        ],
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
    )
    base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    wait_for_server(base_url)
    return proc, base_url


def stop_server(proc):
    proc.terminate()
    proc.wait(timeout=5)


def check(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError("SMOKE TEST FAILED: " + message)
    print("OK: " + message)


def main():
    bearer_token = "smoke-token"
    mail_state = ScriptedMailState()
    mail_port = free_port()
    mail_server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", mail_port), make_handler(mail_state))
    mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    mail_thread.start()
    mail_endpoint = f"http://127.0.0.1:{mail_port}/"

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        # --- Scenario A: operator-staged retry across a restart ---
        db_a = str(Path(tmpdir) / "a.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_A", "--database", db_a)
        run_cli("create-account", "ORG_A", "ACC_A", "person@example.test", "--database", db_a)
        operator = json.loads(run_cli("create-operator", "Ada Support", "--database", db_a))
        run_cli("assign-operator-role", operator["operator_id"], "ORG_A", "agent", "--database", db_a)

        proc, base_url = start_server(db_a, bearer_token, mail_endpoint)
        try:
            status, body = http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/start",
                {"organization": "ORG_A", "email": "person@example.test"},
            )
            check(status == 202, f"recovery/start returned {status}")
            request_id = body["request_id"]
            original_token = mail_state.calls[-1][1]

            status, ticket = http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/admin/tickets",
                {"linked_request_id": request_id, "operator_id": operator["operator_id"], "subject": "Locked out"},
                bearer_token=bearer_token,
            )
            check(status == 201, f"admin/tickets returned {status}: {ticket}")

            calls_before = len(mail_state.calls)
            status, staging = http_json(
                "POST", f"{base_url}/recovery/requests/{request_id}/retry",
                {"operator_id": operator["operator_id"]},
                bearer_token=bearer_token,
            )
            check(status == 201 and staging["result"] == "reserved", f"stage retry: {status} {staging}")
            check(len(mail_state.calls) == calls_before, "staging route sent no mail")
        finally:
            stop_server(proc)

        proc, base_url = start_server(db_a, bearer_token, mail_endpoint)
        try:
            calls_before = len(mail_state.calls)
            status, body = http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=bearer_token,
            )
            check(status == 200, f"notifications/retry returned {status}: {body}")
            new_calls = mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            check(len(new_calls) == 1, f"expected exactly one delivery, got {new_calls}")
            check(new_calls[0] == ("person@example.test", original_token), f"unexpected delivery: {new_calls[0]}")
            check(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"] == "sent", f"unexpected delivery_status: {body}")
        finally:
            stop_server(proc)

        # --- Scenario B: ordinary failed notice across a restart ---
        db_b = str(Path(tmpdir) / "b.db")
        run_cli("create-org", "ORG_B", "--database", db_b)
        run_cli("create-account", "ORG_B", "ACC_B", "other@example.test", "--database", db_b)

        mail_state.push_failure()
        proc, base_url = start_server(db_b, bearer_token, mail_endpoint)
        try:
            calls_before = len(mail_state.calls)
            status, body = http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/start",
                {"organization": "ORG_B", "email": "other@example.test"},
            )
            check(status == 202 and body["delivery_status"] == "queued_for_retry", f"recovery/start: {status} {body}")
            original_token_b = mail_state.calls[calls_before][1]
        finally:
            stop_server(proc)

        proc, base_url = start_server(db_b, bearer_token, mail_endpoint)
        try:
            calls_before = len(mail_state.calls)
            status, body = http_json(
                "POST", base_url + "/recovery/notifications/retry", {},
                bearer_token=bearer_token,
            )
            check(status == 200, f"notifications/retry returned {status}: {body}")
            new_calls = mail_state.calls[calls_before:]
            check(len(new_calls) == 1, f"expected exactly one delivery, got {new_calls}")
            check(new_calls[0] == ("other@example.test", original_token_b), f"unexpected delivery: {new_calls[0]}")
            check(body["retried"][0]["delivery_status"] == "sent", f"unexpected delivery_status: {body}")
        finally:
            stop_server(proc)

    mail_server.shutdown()
    mail_thread.join(timeout=5)
    mail_server.server_close()
    print("SMOKE TEST PASSED")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
